    73	## 2. Behaviour
    74	
    75	The simulation engine ([mine/engine/](mine/engine/)) steps the whole mine five times a second. Each step
    76	covers 12 seconds of mine time, so mine time runs **60× faster than real time: one real minute is one mine
    77	hour**. The clock is published as `kpi.sim_time_h`. The engine publishes every state change to Ditto as
    78	Ditto-protocol `merge` commands over MQTT (about 28 commands per second in total).

    80	| Process | Model | Code |
    81	|---|---|---|

    83	| Haul cycle | Queue -> spot -> load (bucket passes × swing time) -> haul -> dump queue (2 bays) -> dump -> return; one truck at a time per shovel | `simulation.py` |
    84	| Loading | Swing time from fragmentation and cold-weather hydraulics | `models/shovel.py` |
    85	| Blasting | Kuz-Ram X50/X80 from powder factor | `models/blast.py` |
    86	| Crushing, grinding | Crusher capacity; SAG throughput from feed size, ore hardness (Axb) and available power, limited by the ball mills in service; Bond P80; mills draw their available power unless starved | `models/comminution.py`, `simulation.py` |
    87	| Flotation | Constant-tails recovery; grind (P80) and residence-time penalties | `models/flotation.py` |
    88	| Stockpiles | Mass and grade balance (well-mixed) for ROM, crushed, high-grade and waste piles; mass is conserved | `models/stockpile.py` |
    89	| Reliability | Weibull wear-out mode with a condition signal, plus random faults; all-causes MTBF from the reference table | `models/reliability.py` |
    90	| Dust | US EPA AP-42 unpaved-road PM10 on truck vehicle-km; watering only above 0 °C | `models/dust.py` |
    91	| Weather | Temperature, wind and visibility toward scenario targets | `models/weather.py` |
    92	| Economics, energy | Net smelter revenue, costs, diesel and grid energy, CO₂ | `models/economics.py`, `modules/energy.py` |
    93	
    94	#### Interlinked processes
    95	
    96	Trucks deliver ore to the ROM pad at the grade of the face they loaded. The crusher
    97	draws the ROM pad, plus high-grade ore when grade control asks for it, into the crushed-ore stockpile. The SAG
    98	mill draws that stockpile at a rate set by fragmentation, hardness, power and the ball mills in service.
    99	Flotation recovery then follows the feed grade and grind. Pit-side changes reach the plant only through the
   100	stockpiles. That is why haulage scenarios hit "ore mined" first and plant KPIs later.
   101	
   102	#### Back-pressure
   103	
   104	The coupling also runs from plant to pit:
   105	- the crusher stops when the crushed-ore stockpile is full;
   106	- ore trucks wait at the dump when the ROM pad (150 kt) is full.
   107	
   108	The engine checks that mass is conserved (`test_ore_mass_balance_closes`).
   109	
   110	#### Realistic constraints
   111	
   112	Examples:
   113	- one truck at a time under a shovel;
   114	- two dump bays;
   115	- winter speed caps;
   116	- no road watering below 0 °C;
   117	- crusher, mill and stockpile capacities;
   118	- one ball mill down cuts the grinding circuit to 60 % of its capacity;
   119	- fume re-entry times after blasting;
   120	- a closed ramp forces a 2.7 km detour;
   121	- with every shovel on a route down, trucks wait;
   122	- only the two electric-drive trucks can use a trolley line.
   123	
   124	#### Shadow baseline
   125	
   126	The engine runs a second simulation that never receives scenarios. Each time a scenario
   127	is applied or undone, the baseline restarts as an exact copy of the live mine at that moment, including
   128	stockpiles, equipment states and random-number streams. From then on the two differ only because of the
   129	scenario. Each machine also draws its failure times from its own random stream seeded by its name, so both
   130	runs see the same breakdowns. The `kpi` twin publishes `current_*`, `baseline_*` and `delta_*_pct` for
   131	16 KPIs (including grinding energy in kWh per tonne milled). Right after a click every delta is zero, and right after Undo they return to zero. Rate KPIs (ore mined,
   132	diesel, grid energy, haul cycle) are one-mine-hour moving averages, so they move over about a minute of real time.

   144	| Truck fleet availability | 92.6 % | 88-92 % target range [T9], §8.1 |
   145	| Truck haul cycle | 24 min | ~22 min implied by the published fleet plan [S3], §2.5 |

     1	# Kyzyl-Tas - a digital twin of an open-pit copper mine on OpenEgiz
     2	
     3	Kyzyl-Tas is a fictional open-pit copper-gold mine with a 30 Mt/a concentrator. Its equipment, process
     4	capacities, grades and costs are taken from public data for Kazakhstan's Bozshakol and Aktogay operations
     5	(sources in [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md#data-and-assumptions)). Every mine object is an Eclipse Ditto twin
     6	on the OpenEgiz platform. A physics-based simulation engine drives the twins over MQTT. A 3D web interface
     7	reads them back from the platform and runs what-if scenarios.
     8	
     9	## Start
    10	
    11	On a clean Ubuntu 24.04 machine with Docker Engine and Compose v2.20+ (the user must be in the `docker` group),
    12	from the repository root:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y make
    16	make up
    17	```
    18	
    19	`make up` starts the OpenEgiz platform and the mine together. The first run downloads about 2.5 GB of images
    20	and takes several minutes. When it finishes it prints the addresses below. No other step is needed.
    21	
    22	Optional end-to-end check of the running stack (platform and mine):
    23	
    24	```bash
    25	make smoke
    26	```
    27	
    28	## What to open
    29	
    30	| Address | What it is | Login |
    31	|---|---|---|
    32	| **http://localhost:8000** | **Kyzyl-Tas 3D mine: live twins, KPIs, event log, what-if scenarios, twin model** | none |
    33	| http://localhost:3000 | Grafana: mine dashboard "Kyzyl-Tas Mine - KPIs vs baseline" (home page) | none to view |
    34	| http://localhost:3000/a/ertis-opentwins-app/twins | OpenEgiz **Twins** / **Types** pages (all mine twins, hierarchy) | `admin` / printed by `make up` (also in `deploy/compose/.env`) |
    35	| http://localhost:8080/api/2 | Ditto API | `ditto` / printed by `make up` |
    36	
    37	## A two-minute tour
    38	
    39	1. Open http://localhost:8000. Haul trucks move in the pit and the mine clock runs at 60× (one real minute is
    40	   one mine hour). The right panel shows live KPIs, each next to the value of a parallel baseline run.
    41	2. In **What-if scenarios**, click **Shovel S2 failure**. Within about a minute:
    42	   - shovel S2 turns red in the 3D view and on the minimap;
    43	   - its trucks are re-dispatched to S1 and the event log records the chain;
    44	   - ore mined and ore grade fall against the baseline;
    45	   - grade control starts reclaiming the high-grade stockpile (highlighted in 3D).
    46	3. Click **↺ Undo - back to baseline**. Every scenario field returns to its default, S2 returns to service and
    47	   the comparison restarts from zero.
    48	4. Open **Twin model** (top right of the 3D view) to browse all twins, or click any machine for its live data.
    49	   **Custom what-if** at the top of the scenario panel sets the scenario twin's values directly: shovel out,
    50	   trucks parked, crusher, powder factor, dispatch, temperature, ore hardness, mill power, road condition, copper price.
    51	
    52	Each scenario and module is described in [SUBMISSION.md](SUBMISSION.md), with how to see it and how to undo it.

    54	## How it is built
    55	
    56	```
    57	mine-engine (Python simulation)
    58	   │  Ditto protocol "merge" commands, MQTT topic telemetry/<twin>
    59	   ▼
    60	Mosquitto ──► Eclipse Ditto (87 twins, namespace kz.kyzyltas.mine) ──► MQTT events ──► Telegraf ──► InfluxDB
    61	                 ▲                    │                                                              │
    62	                 │ PATCH scenario     │ REST + server-sent events                                    │ Flux
    63	                 │                    ▼                                                              ▼
    64	              mine-ui (nginx + React/three.js) ◄──────────────────────────────────────────── history
    65	```

    68	  drills, crusher, conveyors, mills, flotation, tailings, stockpiles, fans, substation, weather station,

  "stdout": "model is consistent rather than proving it independently. The copper per tonne, fleet availability and
failure count are produced by the simulation. Equipment failures are random, so a single week can differ
(one mill outage of a day lowers that week's mill feed by several percent).

## 3. Visualization

The interface at http://localhost:8000 is a React/three.js application, built into
[mine/ui/dist/](mine/ui/dist/) and served by nginx. It reads twins only from the platform:
- Ditto REST for the catalogue;
- Ditto server-sent events for live changes;
- InfluxDB for history.

It shows:
- 3D scene: the open pit with its benches and two ramps, trucks moving and coloured by haul-cycle state,
  shovels labelled with their face grade, and the plant cluster with stockpiles;
- dust along the haul ramps, whose density follows the twins' haul-road PM10 (fewer particles in performance mode);
- affected equipment highlighted while a scenario runs (broken shovels from their twin state; scenario areas such as
  a closed ramp or the trolley line from the scenario twin);
- weather from the weather twin: snow and denser haze when its temperature and condition call for them;
- mine clock: simulated day and time, 60× real time, starting at 07:00 (day-shift start), with a night tint;
- 2D minimap of equipment positions and states;
- Twin model view (hierarchy, types, live states);
- inspector: click any truck, shovel, plant unit or label to see that twin's live features and relations;
- KPI cards and a baseline-versus-current table, grouped into pit, plant, and economics and energy, plus a
  crushed-ore buffer gauge (hours of mill feed at the SAG mill's rated rate);
- scenario banner with the causal chain and the live key indicators, each marked once the twins confirm it;
- causal event log;
- scenario panel with **↺ Undo - back to baseline**.

Software WebGL is enough: no GPU is required, and a performance mode reduces effects automatically when the
frame rate drops.

A Grafana dashboard, **"Kyzyl-Tas Mine - KPIs vs baseline"**, is Grafana's home page and is readable without
login. It shows the history of the main KPIs from InfluxDB, live mine against the shadow baseline.

## 4. Modules

Each module makes a decision on its own while the mine runs, and its result is written to twin features.

### 4.1 Dispatch and grade control: the fleet-management system (Haulage and Dispatch; Geology and Ore Quality)

#### Dispatch decision

Whenever a truck finishes dumping, the dispatcher sends it to an eligible shovel:
- the one with the shortest queue;
- skipping broken, closed-off or fume-blocked shovels;
- if every shovel on its route is down, the truck waits and asks again.

Code: [mine/engine/modules/dispatch.py](mine/engine/modules/dispatch.py).

#### Grade-control decision

When the ROM pad grade falls below the 0.50 % Cu target, a loader reclaims the
high-grade stockpile (0.65 % Cu) into the crusher feed. It runs in the proportion that restores the target, up
to 800 t/h, and stops when the grade recovers.
Code: [mine/engine/modules/grade_control.py](mine/engine/modules/grade_control.py).

Without the system (`dispatch_policy: "fixed"`, the **Fleet-management system offline** scenario):
- trucks keep their shift-plan shovels;
- a truck whose shovel breaks waits 30 minutes for a supervisor to reassign it by radio ("reassigned by radio"
  in the event log), and the new assignment holds until shift change;
- grade control stops.

#### Where it shows

- each truck's `assigned_shovel` and shovel queue lengths;
- "rerouted" lines in the event log when a shovel breaks;
- `stockpile-hg.reclaim_tph` and `kpi.gc_reclaim_tph`;
- the event lines "grade control: ... reclaiming" and "... stopped".

#### Measured effect

Shovel S2 failure, 12 mine hours, against the shadow baseline, mean of 8 seeded runs
(`tools/validate.py`):

| | Ore mined | Copper output, mine hours 2-12 |
|---|---|---|
| System on | −23 % | −2.8 % |
| System offline (same failure, `dispatch_policy: "fixed"`) | −28 % | −6.6 % |

### 4.2 Predictive maintenance (Equipment Maintenance and Reliability)
- Decision. Every truck carries a coolant-temperature and oil-iron signal that rises as its wear-out
  failure approaches. The engine estimates health and hours to wear-out from that signal; it does not see the
  hidden failure time. With the strategy on (**Predictive maintenance** scenario), crossing the watch level
  raises a work order, and the truck is repaired at the next shift change (5-7 h, no tow) instead of failing
  in service (4-8 h plus a tow). Random faults stay unpredictable.
- Where it shows.
  - estimated `health_pct`, `coolant_temp_c` and `next_pm_due_h` on every truck;
  - "predictive work order raised" and "planned repair" events;
  - `kpi.current_unplanned_failures` against `kpi.baseline_unplanned_failures`, and `kpi.current_planned_repairs`.
- Effect. It pays off over days of mine time. Over 200 mine hours (about 3.3 real hours), summed over 8 seeded
  runs (`tools/validate.py`), unplanned failures fell 23 % (191 against 249, with 73 planned repairs instead), so
  there are fewer in-service breakdowns and tows. Mean fleet availability stayed about the same (92.2 % against
  92.2 %), because planned repairs also take trucks out. The literature reports +2 to +3 points (§8.2, §11-S9); the
  twin's planned-repair time is conservative.
- Code: [mine/engine/models/reliability.py](mine/engine/models/reliability.py), [mine/engine/modules/maintenance.py](mine/engine/modules/maintenance.py).

### 4.3 Energy and CO₂ (Energy)
- What it does. Accounting rather than a control decision:
  - diesel by truck class and haul phase;
  - grid power: crushing, conveying, grinding (mills draw their available power unless starved) and the trolley
    line, whose draw follows the electric trucks under it;
  - both converted into cost and CO₂ with Kazakh tariffs and a 0.80 kg CO₂/kWh grid factor.
- Where it shows. `kpi.current_fuel_l_h`, `kpi.current_energy_kwh_h`, `kpi.current_co2_t_h` and their
  baselines; `substation-01.load_kw`; mill `power_kw`.
- Effect. **Enable trolley assist** puts the two Komatsu 830E trucks on the main ore ramp: fleet diesel
  −4 to −7 %, ore mined up to +5 %. On Kazakhstan's coal-heavy grid the electricity they draw emits about as
  much CO₂ as the diesel it replaces (break-even ≈ 0.64 kg/kWh, §6.4). **Grid power curtailment (mills at 75%)**
  cuts grid energy and CO₂ 13-23 % together with output.
